title: Killing Time
text: “Certainly, I’ve come to understand that much over the course of this journey. If the savior and god worshipped as a hero were to actually come and help with something like this, it would be an enormous relief—but one can’t simply fix things through prayer alone…”

Big Sister’s parent said this to Older Sister, looking troubled, I say. Evidently unaware of certain things. Still, Big Sister’s parent was remarkably dry when it came to hero worship. Big Sister and the others had quite a bit of faith in heroes. In fact, they called us “-sama” at a strikingly high frequency whenever anything came up. How should I put it… Big Sister’s parent might actually be a believer of the Dragon faith from Shieldfreeden. Worth keeping an eye on, indeed.
“Speaking of hero-sama, wasn’t there also some legend about a calamity called a Wave that signals the end of the world?”
“Sadeena?”
Big Sister’s parent tilted their head as if to say, why bring that up now? Brows furrowed, as though trying to convey something important.
“…If Sadeena is this concerned about it, I suppose I could look into it, but are you sure?”
Sharp instincts, I’d say. They seemed inclined to trust Older Sister’s roundabout prompting. Confirming the matter.
“That’s right. If I recall, there was talk of an hourglass starting to move.”

“Ah… I’ve heard tales about something foretelling the arrival of an impending calamity, though I’m not sure how much truth there is to it… I should at least convey the idea to the feudal lord as a precaution. Yes. Thank you, Sadeena.”
Thanked by Big Sister’s parent, Older Sister seemed a touch embarrassed. A rare expression, quite different from how she acts with Father.
“Yes… We mustn’t let Raphtalia-chan and the others worry.”

Apparently Keel was kicking up a fuss over her parent being restrained. Just a little more patience needed there, I say. Sensing, however vaguely, the circumstances Older Sister couldn’t openly explain, Big Sister’s parent went and reported to Éclair’s parent.
“The Dragon Hourglass? Ah, yes, I recall a report about that before… there was word that it had begun moving…”

Éclair’s parent apparently had some idea about it too. Being a crucial facility for Class Ups, it wasn’t something that could go unnoticed. And yet people hadn’t been on guard about it. Someone had apparently remarked that it was all dismissed as mere fairy tale—that no one truly believed it anymore. Heroes appear now and then, but as for the Waves, that was apparently ancient, weathered lore by comparison.
“…Oh my, so it really has started moving.”

Older Sister chimed in to match Éclair’s parent’s words. Well, in Melromarc, it was difficult for demi-humans and beastmen, Older Sister included, to make use of the Dragon Hourglass. Simply entering the building wasn’t easy, so confirming anything was nearly impossible. Which was precisely why Éclair’s parent—entrusted with managing affairs in the Queen’s absence in place of Trash—was in a position to confirm it.
“…If that legend turns out to be true, wouldn’t it fall right around the time the people of this region are out at sea?”
Hmm? Éclair’s parent furrowed their brow at the possibility. The one who appeared to be Crocodile Guy’s parent narrowed their eyes as well.
“Coincidence…? No, regardless, it was certainly careless of us.”
Éclair’s parent went on, saying they’d forgotten it as mere fairy tale.
“Just to be safe, we should remain on guard regarding that as well. Strengthen security, including the search for missing persons!”

Ohoh. A sound judgment, I say. I was glad Older Sister’s guidance was steadily steering things toward reinforced vigilance against the Wave. Amid all this, hearing that the Dragon Hourglass had begun moving, Big Sister’s parent crossed their arms and groaned.
“Hmm… Regardless, let’s head back to the village. Sadeena, shall we?”
“Sure. Who’d have thought it was actually moving—Older Sister had no idea.”
“Indeed.”

Exchanging such words, Older Sister and the others headed back toward the village. Time passed with troubled expressions still lingering. Ah… this stretch of time was maddening, I say. Was I not wasting it needlessly?

Moment by moment, time slipped away. Not a single second could be wasted, indeed. Even with the looping, this particular stretch of time was new to me, so I had to proceed carefully, considering how best to act. …If Older Sister, thinking I wasn’t nearby, went around leaking secrets and then set sail from the harbor, that would be an absolute disaster, I say. Truly troublesome.

Having pinned things down at the harbor this thoroughly, there was also the option of knocking Older Sister out and spiriting her away to keep her quiet. Consulting with others had indeed been the right call, but… the fact that I couldn’t simply sit still, wondering if there was anything else to be done, was the real trouble here.
“Motoyasu, surely there’s still something you can do, nano?”
That voice was my own, along with…
“You’ve already done what you can do. Stop pulling any more unnecessary stunts.”
“With all this groundwork laid, all that’s left is to wait for the results.”

Words that sounded like something Father and the others might say came to mind. Which side was right, I wonder. Truly, the spirit of the spear loves to torment me, I say. So then, let me list out what might be possible to do between now and the Wave.

1. Go knock Takt flat. Head over to Faubrey and swiftly dispose of Takt and those around him, indeed. As for Wolf, it’s already too late for him—there’s no doubt he’s got claws hidden up his sleeve. The situation is thoroughly black through and through. Now that I think of it, didn’t the Four Saints Church in Faubrey have some device that lights up whenever a hero is summoned and present? Presumably, given that I’m here, it’s safe to assume the thing is already lit. If it isn’t, that would mean the device is broken… or perhaps there’s a possibility that a new Spear Hero besides me could be summoned. Slightly concerning, but judging from what the spirit of the spear has hinted at, that possibility seems low. To begin with, this world exists with me in it precisely because the spirit of the spear arranged various things, so it shouldn’t turn into anything that strange, should it? Back to the matter at hand. The idea is to finish off Takt while I still can. I think about this sometimes, but… finishing him off too early raises the risk of the Seven Star Weapon going into hiding. Not terribly necessary, but letting him swim a little longer wouldn’t hurt either. More importantly… in the current situation, if I take my eyes off things even for a moment, there’s a real chance Keel’s parent—whom I’ve got hidden away—could be discovered, or worse, they could set sail right under my nose. So that’s ruled out. Well, perhaps it wouldn’t hurt to go check on that Four Saints Church matter at least.

2. Secure Filolial-sama. I wonder if Yuki-chan and the others have been restocked by now? Though it’s honestly a bit too soon for that, given how little time has passed since then. But still… ugh, I miss Filolial-sama terribly, indeed. Ever since this loop began, I haven’t gotten to play with Filolial-sama at all, and it’s genuinely starting to suffocate me. This matters more to me than finishing off Takt, honestly. But if I go off to secure them, there’s a chance the fleet could set sail in that gap. About the only thing I can afford to look away from is dealing with Rival.

3. Deal with the Three Heroes Church lot while I still can. This might not be such a bad move either. Quietly hunt down, one by one, the problematic members of the Three Heroes Church that I remember from before. Nobles who tortured Big Sister, for instance. If I also take care of Smoked Meat and that so-called knight commander while I’m at it, things might go more smoothly afterward too. Apparently, once Éclair’s parent dies, a swarm of opportunists comes out of the woodwork to start slave-hunting, so this might be a solid plan. Well, picking them off little by little during spare moments might be the way to go. If I’m only gone an hour or two, I can make it back in time. Let’s assassinate a few silently, under cover of night.
4. Secure funds for compensation while I still can. Frankly, I already have enough valuables on hand, so compensating for the ship isn’t an issue. Already accomplished. Low priority, indeed.

5. Draw pictures of Filo-tan to pass the time. Ohh… given how extremely likely it is that Father won’t be summoned this time around, I won’t get to see her. Filo-taaan. So, pouring my feelings into it, continuing to draw pictures of Filo-tan for now and enduring the wait that way… might not be a bad idea at all.
“Alright! Time to draw Filo-tan, I say.”
“Is that really all you came up with after all that deliberation, the one thing you could actually do right now?”

Father seemed to be saying something like that in my mind, but as it turned out, there wasn’t much more to be done than I’d expected! I’d already handled what needed handling! All that was left now was to lie back and await the fruits of my labor, indeed!
